column1: Competing stakeholder needs, why they cannot both be fully satisfied, and the resulting change in scope or requirements

column5: Why it cannot simply be satisfied both ways

column4: Requester needs to submit a request in as few steps as possible; manager needs richly categorised, structured data to report on open, overdue and resolved work by category
column5: Every additional mandatory capture field increases submission effort for the requester. Optional fields produce incomplete data, which weakens the reporting the manager depends on. Both cannot be maximised.
column7: Keep the mandatory field set minimal (category, location, description) and prompt for additional detail after submission rather than before. Category remains mandatory because reporting cannot function without it.

column4: Requester expects full visibility of the status and handling of their own request; security officer requires restricted visibility and handling of security-concern reports
column5: Full transparency on a security-category request could expose who is investigating, what action is being taken, or details that compromise the response. Restricting it removes the visibility that the whole platform exists to provide.
column7: Security-category requests expose a reduced status set to the requester (received, in progress, closed) with detail and comments restricted to an authorised security role. Drives a role-based access requirement rather than a single shared view.

column4: Technicians want to select work from a shared queue based on their own location and availability; coordinator needs controlled assignment so that ownership and accountability are unambiguous
column5: Open self-selection produces the same duplication and unclear ownership the current process suffers from. Fully centralised assignment removes the technicians' practical knowledge of what they can actually reach and reduces responsiveness.
column7: Coordinator assigns by default; technicians may accept an unassigned request within their own category. Every assignment and status transition records the acting user, so accountability holds under either path.

column4: Manager wants historical request data retained for service-performance analysis; information officer requires personal information to be minimised and not retained longer than necessary
column5: Service-performance trends need history. POPIA requires retention to be justified and limited. Keeping everything indefinitely is not lawful; deleting aggressively destroys the reporting value.
column7: Define a retention period for identifiable request data and retain aggregated, non-identifying statistics beyond it. Retention period is deferred pending confirmation from the information officer.
